panels.title: Running version
panels.description: service.version from the OTel resource. The console does not set it — its target_info carries no service_version label — so this reads 'not reported' rather than a version. Kept in place so the gap stays visible and the header row matches its sibling dashboards; the fix is adding service.version to the console's OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES at deploy, after which this tile starts working with no dashboard change. The cluster-side alternative is unavailable: the Grafana Cloud allowlist keeps only kube_pod_info / kube_pod_start_time / kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total, so there is no kube_pod_container_info to read an image tag from.

panels.title: NATS control plane
panels.description: 1 = the console's NATS connection is up; 0 = down, so the live event feed behind every auto-updating panel in the UI is dead even though the page still serves. Catches the boot-race where the console starts before NATS is reachable and stays deaf until restart. No data reads as disconnected.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Wall-clock age of the most-recently-started console pod (time() - max pod start), from kube-state-metrics. Resets on every deploy or restart; a value that keeps resetting means the pod is cycling. Scoped by namespace, which is what carries the environment for cluster scrapes.

panels.title: Pod restarts
panels.description: Total container restarts across the console's pods in the selected env (kube-state-metrics). Green at 0; any restart turns it red — a crash-loop or OOMKill signal the process-level metrics cannot show.

panels.title: Data fresh (last 1m)
panels.description: 1 when the console pushed telemetry within the last 60s. 0 means the process is not reporting — either it is down, or its OTLP export is broken, which would make every other panel on this page stale without them going obviously empty.

panels.title: Requests / sec
panels.description: HTTP request rate across every route. The console is an HTMX app whose panels poll their own partials, so a steady baseline here with no humans watching is normal; a drop to zero means nothing is polling, which usually means nothing is loading the page.

panels.title: Error rate (5xx)
panels.description: Share of requests answered with a 5xx. Note that /health/ready legitimately returns 503 while the console is waiting on NATS, so a burst here right after a deploy is the readiness gate doing its job rather than a fault — check the NATS tile before chasing it.

panels.title: SSE clients
panels.description: Browsers currently holding the console's server-sent-events stream open — effectively how many console tabs are live. Zero is normal when nobody is watching. This is the console's own take on 'is anyone using me', and the number the SSE fan-out cost scales with.

panels.title: HTTP latency (p50 / p95 / p99)
panels.description: Server-side request latency, in seconds. Reads a flat 2.5 / 4.75 / 4.95 until tripbot-console#337 ships: the histogram was left on the OTel SDK default bucket boundaries, which are spaced for milliseconds, so every seconds-valued observation fell into the single (0, 5] bucket and each quantile was `q * 5` from interpolating inside it rather than a measurement. True mean over that period was 78ms (sum/count). Once the explicit seconds boundaries deploy, a window spanning the deploy shows a one-time step as the old le series stop and the new ones start.

panels.title: Requests / sec by status
panels.description: Request rate split by HTTP status. 304s are the static-asset revalidations and are healthy. 404s on the 'unmatched' route are scanners and stray favicon probes rather than broken links.

panels.title: Requests / sec by route (top 10)
panels.description: The busiest routes. Unlike tripbot's HTTP dashboard, the console does get real route templates (/partials/stream/{platform} rather than an empty label), so this is a genuine per-endpoint view. Expect the /partials/* family to dominate — those are the self-polling panels.

panels.title: SSE clients over time
panels.description: Open server-sent-events connections over time. A sawtooth is normal (tabs open and close); a flat line pinned above zero with nobody watching means connections are not being reaped, which leaks a goroutine and a NATS subscription per stuck client.

panels.title: Fleet health (as the console sees it)
Components reported down
panels.description: How many platform components the console currently reports as down, across every component and platform it watches. This is the console's own view of the fleet, not an independent check — if the console's NATS connection is down, treat this tile as unknown rather than as good news, because a console that cannot hear anything reports nothing down.

panels.title: Components down over time, by component
panels.description: How many platforms each component is down on, over time. Aggregating by component rather than by platform answers the more common question first — 'is obs broken everywhere or just on tiktok' — and keeps the series count at one per component instead of one per pair.

panels.title: Component × platform (current)
panels.description: One tile per component/platform pair the console tracks — six components across the five supported platforms. A pair with no tile is a pair the console is not reporting on at all, which is different from a pair reporting down and usually means that platform's component was never wired up in this environment.

panels.title: Recent errors & warnings
panels.description: Error and warning lines from the console, newest first. Severity comes from the detected_level label (lowercase values), not severity_text.

options.content:
Health overview for the **tripbot-console** binary — the admin live console.

Two things read differently here than on the sibling service-health pages:

- **No platform selector.** The console runs as a single Deployment rather than one instance per platform, so there is nothing to split by. The `service_platform` label on `console_platform_component_up` names the platform each *reported component* belongs to, not the instance doing the reporting.
- **No 'Recent traces' table.** 03/04/05 each carry one; whether the console exports spans to Tempo has not been confirmed, and an unverified trace table renders as an empty panel that reads like a broken service. Add it once there are spans to show.

**Known source-side gaps**, both fixable in the console repo rather than here:

1. `target_info` carries no `service_version`, so the Running version tile reads "not reported". Fix is `service.version` in `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` at deploy.
2. The request-duration histogram carried no usable signal — the SDK's default bucket boundaries are spaced for milliseconds, so seconds-valued observations all landed in one bucket and every quantile was an interpolation artifact (`q * 5`), not a measurement. Fixed at the source in tripbot-console#337. The panel is labelled seconds because the data is seconds, and reads flat until that ships.
